tagline: The drovers' way through Hickory Nut Gap, turkeys and all.
intro: US 74A heads east from the Blue Ridge Parkway through Fairview, over Hickory Nut Gap and on through Hickory Nut Gorge, past Gerton to Bat Cave. Mature trees stand on the hillsides, the high, steep sides of the gorge are covered in a cascade of rocks, trees and rhododendron, and Hickory Nut Creek, also called the Rocky Broad, comes into view.
The route is the drovers' road of 1798, the way farmers took their livestock out of the mountains to market. The livestock was mostly turkeys, along with some geese, hogs and cattle.

moments.title: Little Pisgah Mountain
moments.text: Off to the east stands a 4,412-foot peak that the Cherokee once called Konnatoga.

moments.title: Sherrill's Inn
moments.text: Once the comfort stop for drovers, settlers and Civil War soldiers, the inn that gave the gap its old name of Sherrill's Gap is a private home, visible from the road's wide curves.

moments.title: Gerton
moments.text: The hamlet was called Pump until 1902, when a new postmark misspelled it Rump and the embarrassed residents renamed it after a schoolteacher, Gertrude Freeman, in a modest contraction.
